keyManager.latencyPolicy: Explicit virtual protocol240 nominal cycles; no physical time/KM-edge/crypto claim.

actualNative.description: The unchanged original guest polls READY, executes both original IDLE checks, selects the eFuse source and writes DPA4 then5. It later logs sleep-GPIO/coexistence versions and reaches a currently unsupported COEX clock-divider request before app_main.

contracts: The strict cold/ideal-awake HP domain is explicitly modeled functional availability, checked independently of APB and pre-DPA source; safe PMU target words do not prove physical power or settling. Missing owner, pending reset or unknown input does not grant the domain.

Actual unprovisioned logical eFuse shadow words supply DPA[21:20],CRYPT_CNT[18:16] parity and forced-KM flash/PSRAM bit11. The pure getter does not issue READ_CMD, touch OTP, change IRQ/read-done or create a valid key.

Key Manager release requires actual SRAM PU without PD, local gate, real reset assertion/release, known source/APB/domain and known-off policies. A finite declared virtual240-cycle event supplies completion; constructor/header READY or guest RO writes cannot supply runtime IDLE.
PMU materialization and clock/analog updates publish old/new observations at the same boundary. Input loss cancels a pending event and requires a new reset; restoration does not backfill completion.

CPU reset preserves the autonomous pending event. HP reset clears it at reset_at; raw profile exit drops it and its deadline. Earlier WDT service commits only KM events strictly before the reset; an equal-time reset wins. Subword MMIO cannot bypass that reset barrier or force a control write.
Exact owned refusals are Unsupported/ModelLimit with plain/UnitCost CSR/destination/controller preservation. Adjacent and off-profile unknown words keep their prior mapping.

The small plain/UnitCost guest actually writes power/gate/reset, polls READY, reads STATE once and ORs/writes STATIC. The original unchanged firmware separately executes its two IDLE checks, seen in bounded traces and STATE read count2.

Completed configuration/IDLE history may remain latched while unavailable power/gate/source hides runtime observations; restoring their known qualification can expose that prior IDLE. This bounded invariant with no accepted START is not SRAM retention, physical power-ready or a usable key.
DPA named configuration0..7 is recorded without a divider engine. DPA5 after completion retains digital IDLE/configuration but cannot qualify a new reset event or any crypto/key/START/data consumer.
The pre-integrated modem ICG maps and helper counters do not provide COEX execution, RF/PHY readiness, guest SD-read completion, FAT mount, durable storage or product acceptance.

reviews.scope: Independent read-only owner/glue/seven fixture review; no P1/P2 in the declared virtual scope. READY polling plus single STATE fixture read differs from the original two IDLE loops; no independent execution.
Read-only exact eFuse/awake-domain input and old-WDT/reset-at audit; no physical power-ready inference. Parent subsequent implementation and tests are separately recorded.
Read-only helper same-card/publication/u64 observation review, two source fingerprints stable; no P1/P2, no new runtime execution.

limits: The latest original boundary is a known COEX word with an unsupported nonzero divider. No app_main/FreeRTOS ordinary-watchdog/LCD/buttons/TF or RF/PHY success claim.
These focused LTO=false checks do not replace final native default-LTO workspace CI, controlled CPU comparisons, updated production WASM/browser or fresh product acceptance.
The previous default-release production WASM artifact and platform result were measured before KM/modem/helper integration; they are historical, not validation of this new backend.
Raw logs/private paths are omitted. Original input bytes and measured numeric/log hashes remain unchanged.
